intended_object: The n-th continuous group cohomology H^n_cts(G, X) of a topological group G with coefficients in a topological k-representation X. It is computed after lifting G and X into a common universe. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the name.
explanation: The body applies Mathlib's `continuousCohomology n` to `normalized X`. `normalized X` is the library's `TopRep.ulift`: it replaces G by `ULift G` and the carrier of X by `ULift X`, transported along `ContinuousLinearEquiv.ulift`, with action g • up x = up (g.down • x). So it is canonically isomorphic to X as a topological representation. The lift is needed because Mathlib's recursive homogeneous-cochain construction requires the group and the carrier to be in the same universe. Lifting both to max v w is a purely technical normalization. Mathlib's `continuousCohomology` is the homology of the homogeneous continuous cochain complex: the G-invariants of C(G, C(G, …, C(G, X))) with the standard differential. That is the textbook continuous cohomology. The setting is a topological ring k, a topological group G and an arbitrary TopRep, which matches Mathlib's own generality, so the definition is not too narrow. It is a thin wrapper, but the result is the intended mathematical object up to a canonical universe-lifting isomorphism.
